# Attachment Style Frameworks

## What it is
A family of relational frameworks describing recurring patterns of security, anxiety, avoidance, and closeness regulation.

## Why it matters
This is a starter registry entry for Attachment Style Frameworks. It is structurally valid but should be deepened with better sources, richer claims, and more precise cross-system analysis.

## What it is good for
- placeholder registry coverage
- incremental source collection
- ontology refinement

## Common misuse
- treating a starter entry as fully researched

Attachment frameworks claim to describe recurring relational patterns that shape closeness, safety, and regulation.
Attachment language is highly useful for relationship interpretation but often overgeneralized beyond the contexts that activate it.

Big Five Personality Model
Big Five
OCEAN
Five-Factor Model
FFM
A dimensional trait personality framework typically organized around Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism.
# Big Five Personality Model

## What it is
A broad trait framework organizing personality variation into five major domains.

## Why it matters
In this registry, Big Five functions as one of the strongest empirical anchor layers for synthesis work. It is less thick as an identity language than systems like Enneagram or Human Design, but stronger as a baseline trait scaffold.

## What it is good for
- broad personality description
- baseline trait comparison
- self-reflection
- communication and work-style inference
- synthesis anchoring

## What it is weaker at
- motive language
- identity narrative
- defense strategy
- symbolic meaning
- thick developmental storytelling

## Common misuse
Treating broad traits as a total explanation of a person.

The model organizes personality variation into five broad trait domains.
The framework is intended to describe relatively stable personality traits rather than momentary emotional states.
The Big Five exists as a family of instruments with multiple public and proprietary implementations.
Big Five is one of the best baseline anchor frameworks for a synthesis system because it supplies relatively stable broad trait scaffolding without imposing a thick symbolic identity narrative.
Big Five is weaker as a direct language of motive, defense strategy, or identity narrative than systems like Enneagram, despite being stronger in psychometric grounding.
Broad tendency toward imagination, curiosity, aesthetic sensitivity, intellectual exploration, and preference for novelty and complexity.
Broad tendency toward organization, self-discipline, reliability, and goal-directed behavior.
Broad tendency toward sociability, energetic engagement, positive affect, and stimulation seeking.
Broad tendency toward compassion, cooperation, trust, and concern for social harmony.
Broad tendency toward emotional volatility, stress reactivity, negative affect, and vulnerability.

Enneagram of Personality
Enneagram
Enneagram of Personality Types
A typological framework centered on nine core personality strategies often described in terms of motivation, fear, desire, fixation, defense, and growth/stress patterns.
# Enneagram of Personality

## What it is
A typological framework organized around nine core strategies often described through motives, fears, desires, and defenses.

## Why it matters
In this registry, Enneagram is valuable because it captures identity and motive language that many more psychometric frameworks describe only indirectly. It is also a strong example of a system that is culturally sticky despite a weaker evidence base.

## What it is good for
- motive exploration
- coaching language
- developmental reflection
- relational patterning
- identity narrative analysis

## What it is weaker at
- psychometric grounding
- standardized measurement
- low-interpretation administration
- clean construct commensurability

## Common misuse
Using type as destiny language or as an overconfident total explanation of the person.

The system describes nine core personality strategies or types.
Type descriptions are commonly framed through core motivations, fears, desires, and defensive patterns.
The framework often claims that each type has characteristic growth and stress dynamics.
Enneagram is comparatively strong as a language of motive, defense strategy, and identity narrative even where psychometric grounding remains weak.
Its practical power is partly social and narrative, which also makes it unusually prone to identity capture and practitioner overreach.
A reform-oriented strategy organized around restraint, improvement, and correctness.
A relationship-oriented strategy organized around helpfulness, approval, and connection.
An achievement-oriented strategy organized around performance, image, and adaptation.
An identity-oriented strategy organized around depth, uniqueness, and longing.
A withdrawal-oriented strategy organized around competence, privacy, and cognitive mastery.
A security-oriented strategy organized around vigilance, loyalty, and threat management.
An expansive strategy organized around possibility, stimulation, and avoidance of constriction.
A force-oriented strategy organized around autonomy, intensity, and resistance to control.
A harmony-oriented strategy organized around stability, merger, and conflict minimization.

Myers-Briggs Type Indicator
MBTI
Myers Briggs
A widely used typology framework built around four preference pairs that combine into sixteen type codes.
# Myers-Briggs Type Indicator

## What it is
A typological framework based on four preference pairs that combine into sixteen type codes.

## Why it matters
MBTI is culturally and organizationally important because it functions as a durable shorthand for personality difference, especially in workplace and coaching settings. Its practical stickiness matters even where evidence and construct commensurability remain contested.

## What it is good for
- communication shorthand
- lightweight team discussion
- reflective preference language
- coaching conversation

## What it is weaker at
- trait measurement
- clean construct comparability
- high-stakes decisions
- preserving nuance under binary labels

## Common misuse
Treating type as a hard box or using it for selection and assignment decisions.

The framework organizes people into sixteen type combinations based on four preference pairs.
Type outputs are commonly framed as preferences rather than measures of ability or skill.
The system is presented as deriving from Jungian ideas about psychological type.
The MBTI assessment is not intended for selection or hiring decisions.
MBTI persists because it offers an extremely portable social shorthand for communication and work-style differences.
Its type-coded outputs are often easier to remember than to justify, especially when they are treated as trait measures rather than interpretive preferences.
A preference pair describing orientation toward outer engagement or inner reflection.
A preference pair describing attention to concrete detail or pattern-level possibility.
A preference pair describing decision style in terms of impersonal analysis or value-based consideration.
A preference pair describing preference for structure and closure or openness and spontaneity.
